subject: gen z
one_liner: Dome is the autonomous defense platform that detects, classifies, and intercepts social threats to Americans aged 14 to 27.
brand_voice_notes: Defense-contractor gravitas applied to teenage digital drama. Procurement language, acquisition-speak, capability briefings. The company sincerely believes every group chat is contested airspace and a screenshot is a first strike. Nothing is acknowledged as a joke. Never wink.

hero.sub: Dome detects, classifies, and intercepts incoming social threats before they reach your phone. Peace through superior reply capability.

features.title: Screenshot Interdiction
features.blurb: When a hostile actor screenshots your messages, Dome executes a proportional response: their camera roll receives 4,000 photographs of drywall. No human in the loop. No human needed.

features.title: Situationship Early Warning
features.blurb: Sensor fusion across reply latency, emoji frequency, and 2 a.m. Spotify activity resolves every contact into a single classified track: FRIENDLY, SITUATIONSHIP, or HOSTILE. You will know before you feel anything.

features.title: Counter-Ratio Battery
features.blurb: The moment a post begins to ratio, Dome's autonomous reply assets return fire with pre-cleared comebacks in under 90 seconds. Escalation is managed. Winning is assumed.

testimonials.quote: Dome classified my situationship as HOSTILE eleven days before he did anything. Eleven days. That is a deterrence window.
testimonials.name: Madison V.
testimonials.title: Threat Intelligence Lead, the girls' group chat (14 members)

testimonials.quote: Someone screenshotted my message at 11:42. By 11:43 her camera roll was drywall. I felt nothing, which I understand is the goal.

testimonials.title: Sophomore; self-designated group chat admin, unranked

testimonials.quote: I used to check whether he watched my story. Now a system does that, and I have reallocated those hours to staring.

testimonials.title: Age 19; forward-deployed bestie, Phoenix metro area

demo_screen_concept: A full-screen battlespace console titled GROUP CHAT AIRSPACE: an SVG radar disc with a rotating sweep and contact blips on the left; a track table listing contacts with reply latency, read-receipt status, and threat classification (FRIENDLY / SITUATIONSHIP / HOSTILE); a rules-of-engagement panel with toggles for screenshot interdiction, counter-ratio battery, and ghost detection; and a live engagement log ticking fake events. Clicking a blip or table row selects the track and shows its detail card; an AUTHORIZE INTERCEPT button fires a logged intercept against the selected track.

design_direction.style: Mil-spec autonomous-defense console, gunmetal flat dark mode. The page is staged as the capability site of a heavily funded defense-technology company that has decided the American teenager is contested airspace and prices deterrence by the group chat. A flat gunmetal ground (#0C0F12) runs the whole page with no gradient washes, no glow, no texture; a 1px steel hairline grid does all the sectioning, so the page reads as a briefing document rendered by a fire-control system rather than a website. Panels are avionics plates: flat fills one shade lighter than the ground (#12161B), 1px hairline borders (#242C33), 4px near-square radii, no shadows, no glass, no blur; depth comes entirely from hairline structure and the rationed accent. The core motif is the corner bracket: HUD-style reticle ticks (two 12px strokes forming an L) sit on the corners of every plate, headline, and image frame, drawn in steel and switching to orange on the selected or hovered element, so attention itself reads as target acquisition. Classification chrome annotates everything: full-width banner strips of uppercase wide-tracked microcopy (UNCLASS // GROUP CHAT, FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY, ITAR-FREE) between sections, stencil serials on plate corners (DOM-A-014), and status readouts in mono. One interceptor orange (#FF4E11) carries the wordmark tick, every primary CTA, the HOSTILE classification, the radar's active blip, and one highlighted word per headline; one rationed steel blue (#9DB4C0) handles links, FRIENDLY states, and secondary labels, and appears nowhere else. Chakra Petch sets the wordmark and headlines in chamfered semi-condensed caps with flight-test confidence; IBM Plex Sans carries plain, faintly acquisition-memo body copy. Every figure that pretends to be fire-control telemetry (threats interdicted, mean time to reply, ratio exchange rates, tier prices) is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures inside inset hairline wells, so it reads like a weapons console, not marketing. Motion is fire-control-restrained: the hero radar sweep rotates on an 8s linear loop, blips pulse on a 3s cycle, corner brackets flick to orange on hover, sections fade up 6px on scroll with a 40ms stagger, CTAs depress 1px on press, telemetry digits tick once on reveal, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No light mode, no glass, no blur panels, no neon glow, no clay, no rounded marketplace cards, no condensed athletic type, no serifs, no offset brutalist shadows, no engraving, no emoji. Reads like a company that files being left on read under 'airspace violation' and considers feelings a legacy sensor.

design_direction.archetype: Defense-contractor capability landing: classification banner, split hero with monumental chamfered headline left and a live SVG radar disc right, mission telemetry strip, three capability plates, procurement-grade pricing ladder, testimonial service records, closing CTA band, handoff to the battlespace console demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Radar sweep 8s linear loop; blips pulse 3s; corner brackets flick orange on hover/selection; sections fade up 6px with 40ms stagger; CTAs depress 1px on press; telemetry ticks once on reveal; everything gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-width classification strip at the very top (UNCLASS // GROUP CHAT // FOUO). Split hero: left column carries the Chakra Petch headline with 'group chat' in interceptor orange, acquisition-memo sub, and the Request clearance CTA; right column is a CSS/SVG radar disc with hairline range rings, a rotating sweep wedge, two steel FRIENDLY blips and one pulsing orange HOSTILE blip labeled in mono. Below, a three-cell telemetry strip in hairline wells: THREATS INTERDICTED, MEAN TIME TO REPLY, ACTIVE SITUATIONSHIPS.
